text: A circle does not touch a(nother) circle at more than one point, whether they touch internally or externally.
For, if possible, let circle $ABDC$$^{\,\dag}$ touch circle $EBFD$---first of all, internally---at more than one point, $D$ and $B$.
assertion: circle ABDC touches circle EBFD internally at more than one point D and B

frame.supposition: circle $ABDC$ touches circle $EBFD$---first of all, internally---at more than one point, $D$ and $B$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: circle $ABDC$$^{\,\dag}$ touch circle $EBFD$---first of all, internally---at more than one point, $D$ and $B$

text: And let the center $G$ of circle $ABDC$ be found [Prop.~3.1],
and (the center) $H$ of $EBFD$ [Prop.~3.1].
Thus, the (straight-line) joining $G$ and $H$ will fall on $B$ and $D$ [Prop.~3.11].
assertion: the straight-line joining G and H falls on B and D

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the (straight-line) joining $G$ and $H$ will fall on $B$ and $D$

text: Let it fall like $BGHD$ (in the figure).
And since point $G$ is the center of circle $ABDC$, $BG$ is equal to $GD$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $G$ is the center of circle $ABDC$

text: Thus, $BG$ (is) greater than $HD$.
Thus, $BH$ (is) much greater than $HD$.
assertion: BH is much greater than HD

text: Again, since point $H$ is the center of circle $EBFD$, $BH$ is equal to $HD$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $H$ is the center of circle $EBFD$

text: But it was also shown (to be) much greater than it. The very thing (is) impossible.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: it was also shown (to be) much greater than it

text: Thus, a circle does not touch a(nother) circle internally at more than one point.
assertion: a circle does not touch another circle internally at more than one point

frame.closes: circle $ABDC$ touches circle $EBFD$---first of all, internally---at more than one point, $D$ and $B$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a circle does not touch a(nother) circle internally at more than one point

text: So, I say that neither (does it touch) externally (at more than one point).
For, if possible, let circle $ACK$ touch circle $ABDC$ externally at more than one point, $A$ and $C$.
assertion: circle ACK touches circle ABDC externally at more than one point A and C

frame.supposition: circle $ACK$ touches circle $ABDC$ externally at more than one point, $A$ and $C$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: circle $ACK$ touch circle $ABDC$ externally at more than one point, $A$ and $C$

text: And let $AC$ be joined.

Therefore, since two points, $A$ and $C$, be taken at random on the circumference of each of the circles $ABDC$ and $ACK$, the straight-line joining the points will fall inside each (circle) [Prop.~3.2].
assertion: the straight-line AC falls inside each of the circles ABDC and ACK

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: two points, $A$ and $C$, be taken at random on the circumference of each of the circles $ABDC$ and $ACK$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the straight-line joining the points will fall inside each (circle)

text: But, it fell inside $ABDC$, and outside $ACK$ [Def.~3.3].
assertion: AC fell inside ABDC and outside ACK

text: The very thing (is) absurd.
Thus, a circle does not touch a(nother) circle externally at more than one point.
assertion: a circle does not touch another circle externally at more than one point

frame.closes: circle $ACK$ touches circle $ABDC$ externally at more than one point, $A$ and $C$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a circle does not touch a(nother) circle externally at more than one point

text: And it was shown that neither (does it) internally.
assertion: it was shown that a circle does not touch another circle internally at more than one point

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: it was shown that neither (does it) internally

text: Thus, a circle does not touch a(nother) circle at more than one point, whether they touch internally or externally. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
